:
Petitioners filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the death of deceased C. Sidda Reddy, in road traffic accident.

02. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
2.1.
It is stated that, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children of deceased, respectively.
Deceased was serving as a Teacher in Zilla Parishath High School, at Angallu.
On 12.02.2019, after attending work in school, deceased has left Angallu to go Madanapalle.
It is contended that, he was proceeding on Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No. AP-03- BJ-8096.
Near Central Dhaba, on Madanapalle-Angallu road, at about 5.20 p.m., driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No. NL-01-Q-0228 has caused accident and dashed the deceased from behind.
As a result of impact, he fell down and sustained injuries in head and all over the body and he died on spot.
Immediately, he was shifted to District Government Hospital, Madanapalle and he was declared dead by Medical officer.
2.2. Deceased was aged about 56 years at the time of accident.
Deceased was a Teacher in Government school and he was earning Rs.86,000/- per month.
Petitioners are dependents of the Smt. V. Rajeswari @ C. Rajeswaramma vs Sandeep Wadhwa On Of Raj Krishan on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148024734/

sentences.text: 2 deceased and due to untimely death of C.Sidda Reddy, petitioners have lost loving members of the family and also lost financial support.
2.3. The jurisdictional Mudivedu police have registered a case against the driver of offending vehicle in Cr. No.11/2019, under Sec.304 (A) of IPC and Sec.134(b) r/w Sec.187 of M.V. Act.
1 st respondent is the RC owner of offending vehicle and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
On the date of accident the insurance policy of vehicle was in force.
With these averments they pray to allow the petition.
03. Respondent No.1 has neither filed written statement nor contested the claim of petitioners.
04. Respondent No. 2-Insurance Company has filed written statement contending that, the petition is not maintainable.
It is contended that, owner of offended vehicle has allowed unauthorized person to drive the vehicle and driver of said vehicle had no valid and effective D.L., as on the date of accident.
It is contended that, Lorry in question was plying in place of accident without having valid permit.
4.1. Involvement of offended vehicle is denied.
The age and income of the deceased is denied.
It is contended that, deceased was riding the motorcycle unmindful without wearing helmet and the accident was occurred only due to negligence of deceased.
Owner and insurer of motor cycle are the necessary parties to the case.
It is stated that, claimants are permanent residents of Andhra Pradesh and respondent No.1 is residing at Delhi and therefore, this Tribunal has no jurisdiction to entertain the case.
With these averments, it prays to dismiss the petition.
05. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
: I S S U E S:
1. Whether respondent No.2 proves that the Tribunal has no territorial jurisdiction to try the case?

2. Whether petitioners proves that C. Sidda Reddy has died on 12.02.2019 due to the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of driver of Lorry bearing Registration No.NL-01-Q-0228 as stated in the petition?
3. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves alleged contributory negligence on the part of deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the reliefs sought for?
5. What order or award?
06. In order to prove the case, Petitioner No.2 was examined as PW.1.
One witness was examined as P.W:2.
Exhibits were marked as Ex.P.1 to 15.
Learned counsel for Respondent No.2 has cross-examined Pw:1 and 2.
Respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as R.W.1 and two documents were marked as Ex.R.1 and 2.

My findings to the above referred Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 :- In the Negative.

Issue No.2 :- In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 :- In the Negative.
 Issue No.4 :- In Partly Affirmative.
 Issue No.5 :- As per final order for the following.

:REASONS:
09.
ISSUE No.1 :- This is a petition under Sec.166 of M.V. Act.

It is the specific plea of the Insurance Company that, the Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try the petition on hand since petitioners are permanent residents of Andhra Pradesh State and R.C. owner of the vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 is residing at Delhi.
It is further argued that Insurance Policy was issued by Respondent no:2 at Delhi .
10. Territorial Jurisdiction:
The claim petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act can be initiated in any of the following places.

1) The place where the accident has taken place, 2) the place where the claimants are residing or 3) the place where any one of the respondents in the proceedings is residing or 4) in the place where the policy to offending vehicle is issued from the insurer of the vehicle, as observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a case reported in 2017 (1) KCCR 511 (Anitha and Others Vs. Ravindranath and Another and, 2). Hanumanth vs Shankar Satappa Wali (WP no:114729-2019), 3) Mantoo Sarkar Vs Oriental Insurance co. Ltd. And others (Civil appeal no 7318-2017 arising out of special leave petition civil no; 18201 0f 2007).

Under these circumstances, the Tribunal has Territorial Jurisdiction to adjudicate the petition on hand.
Hence, issue no: 1 is answered in the negative.
12. ISSUE no: 2 and 3:-
For the sake of convenience, these issues have been taken up for common discussion as hereunder.
It is the specific plea of the insurance company that the incident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased.

sentences.text: The petitioners herein are legal heirs of deceased C.Siddareddy.

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 12.02.2019, at about 5.20 p.m., the deceased was proceeding on motor cycle as a rider and he met with the road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of lorry in question and succumbed to the injuries on spot.
14.
To prove their contention, petitioners have lead oral and documentary evidence.
PW-1- 2nd petitioner, who is the son of deceased has filed affidavit by way of examination in chief and reiterated the averments made in the petition.

15. If, the evidence of PW.1 is perused along with Ex.P.1- The charge sheet, Ex.P-9 FIR , ExP-10: The complaint, Ex.P.11- The postmortem report of deceased, it is abundantly clear that the accident was occurred on 12.02.2019 at about 5.20 p.m., on Angallu-Madanapalle road.
16. The charge sheet has been submitted against the driver of offending vehicle.
The spot of accident and death of C.Siddreddy in accident are not in dispute at all.
The involvement of two vehicles in the accident, date and timings of incident are not in dispute.
17. It is the specific defence of the Insurance Company that, deceased- the rider of motor cycle was not wearing helmet and therefore, he sustained grievous injuries in the head.

In cross examination,
Pw.1 has denied that deceased had no valid DL or riding the vehicle without wearing helmet.
18. No positive evidence is available on record to believe that deceased was not wearing the helmet at the time of incident.
It is specific plea of the Insurance Company that, the accident is occurred due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
No positive evidence is placed on record by Insurance Company to establish that, the incident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased.

19. The insurance company has not examined the rider of offending vehicle or ocular witness to the accident or Investigating officer to prove that, there was absolute negligence on the part of rider i.e.,
the deceased.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative and issue no:3 in the negative.
20. ISSUE No.4:-
Age: In the petition it is shown as the age of deceased was 56 years at the time of death.
Ex. P-7
is the Aadhaar Card of deceased and in this document his date of birth is shown as 5/4/1962.
In ExP:8, the ration card of deceased, the date of birth is shown as 08/15/1964.
In ExP:15, the service book of deceased the date of birth is shown as 05/04/1962.
The accident was occurred on 12.02.2019.
Hence, on the basis of Service book, produced by Pw:2 the age of deceased is considered as 57 years at the time of his death.
21. Income of the deceased:- Respondent No.2 has disputed the income of deceased.
Pw:1 has deposed that deceased was a teacher in government school.
ExP:2 and 3 are the Pay slip and bank statement of the deceased.

To prove, the occupation and income of the deceased, petitioners have examined Y. Vishwanath Reddy, School Assistant at ZP High school, Angallu, Madanapalli Smt. V. Rajeswari @ C. sentences.text: This witness has produced the authorization letter, salary certificate and service record of the deceased at ExP:12 to 15 respectively.

22. Cross examination of Pw:2 reveals that legal heirs of deceased have received Rs.1,40,000/-
under Group Insurance.
ExP:13 is the salary certificate of deceased and perusal of same reveals that total salary of deceased was Rs. 86,283/-.
As per salary certificate, Rs.14,502/- has been deducted in salary towards GPF/PPF, APGLI, Group Insurance, profession Tax, EHF, APGLI loan.
The petitioners have not produced I.T. Returns submitted by the deceased.
The amount deducted towards income tax is not clearly shown in ExP:13.
Pw:2 deposed that deceased was paying Income Tax of Rs. 80,000/- per annum and it is not denied by the petitioners.
So, annual income of the deceased is Rs. 86,283 x12 = Rs.10,35,396/-.
From annual income of the deceased Income Tax of Rs.80,000/- and profession Tax of Rs.2,400/- is to be deducted.
So, the annual income of the deceased after deduction of Income Tax and Professional Tax is Rs.9,52,996/-.
23. Dependants:- Evidence of Pw:2 reveals that after the accident, no employment has been given to the Dependants of the deceased on compassionate ground.
It is an admitted fact that 3 rd petitioner is a married daughter of deceased.
Petitioner no;2 and 3 have got no jobs.
Therefore, they are the Dependants of deceased.
24. It is the specific plea of Insurance Company that, petitioner No. 2 and 3 were not at all depending on the income of the deceased as they are adults and major children.
Counsel for petitioners argued that, major sons and married daughters of deceased are dependents and they are also entitled for the compensation.
25. It is significant to note that, petitioners herein belong to middle class family.
P.W.1 is a housewife.
Petitioner no: 3 is married daughter of deceased.
Petitioner No.2 is unmarried son of deceased and he is unemployed.
Therefore, whatever the small income being earned by the deceased would matters a lot to this family to lead the livelihood in better way.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.

26. Even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency,
physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth,
which can never be equated in terms of the money.
Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency.
Hence, the very contention of the Insurance Company cannot be accepted.
My reason is supported by the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others.

sentences.text: Hence, Petitioners no:1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.

Keeping in view of the 3 dependents of deceased in the case on hand,
1/3rd amount is to be deducted toward personal expenses.
27. Deceased was aged about 57 years at the time of accident.
So, annual income of deceased is taken at Rs.9,52,996/- which would meet the ends of justice.

Sarala Verma's case 2009 ACJ 1298 (SC),
may also be applied to persons who were self-employed or were engaged on fixed wages.

Hence, I Smt. V. Rajeswari @ C. Rajeswaramma vs Sandeep Wadhwa On Of Raj Krishan on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148024734/
6 am of the opinion that it would meet the ends of justice if increase in 15% is taken into consideration for determining the income of the deceased.

sentences.text: By applying the principles of above ruling 15% has to be added to annual income of deceased, which comes to Rs.1,42,949/-.
So, annual income of deceased is taken at Rs.10,95,945/-, which would meet the ends of justice.
From this his personal living expenses which should be 1/3rd of Rs.10,95,945/- has to be deducted.

Thereby, the actual annual income will come to Rs.10,95,945 - Rs.3,65,315/- =Rs.7,30,630/-.
28.
As the deceased was 57 years old at the time of death, the multiplier of 09 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.7,30,630/- x 09 = Rs.65,75,670/- for loss of dependency.
29. Rs.15,000/- is awarded for funeral expenses.

In view of decision of Hon'ble Apex court of Karnataka reported in a case between United India Insurance co.Ltd. Vs Siddalingaiah and others (MFA no: 1322-2017 MV), Rs.15,000/- is awarded for loss of estate.

sentences.text: Rs.40,000/- each is awarded for loss of spousal and parental consortium.

The details of compensation amount is as under:
 S.N Heads Rs.
 1. Towards loss of Rs. 65,75,670/-
 Dependency  2. Loss of spousal and Rs. 1,20,000/-
 parental consortium.

40,000 X 3  3. Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 4.

Funeral expense Rs. 15,000/-
 5.
Towards Transportation Rs. 5,000/-
The employer of the deceased has paid the petitioners Rs.1,40,000/- under Group Insurance.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.67,30,670 - Rs.1,40,000= Rs.
65,90,670/-.
31. Driving License & Permit :- No allegation made in Charge sheet submitted by IO that, driver of vehicle in question was driving without valid and effective DL.
No positive has taken by R-2 to prove that owner of the vehicle has allowed unauthorized person to drive the vehicle or vehicle had no valid permit.
Hence, it is held that, the driver of offended vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
32. Insurance Policy:- It is admitted fact that, insurance policy of offended vehicle was valid and effective at the time of alleged accident.
ExR:2 is the insurance policy of the vehicle in question.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Therefore, R-2 being insurer of the vehicle shall pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, I answer Issue No.4 is in partly affirmative .

sentences.text: In view of discussion made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.65,90,670/-
(Rupees Sixty Five Lakhs, Ninety Thousand, Six Hundred and Seventy Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

Respondent No:2 shall pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount to the petitioners in the court within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60%, petitioner no: 2 and 3 are entitled for 20% each with interest.

50% of share of petitioners with interest is to be paid to them through E-payment,
after due identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their names in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on desktop, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced in the open court by me on 19th day of April, 2023).

It is the specific plea of the Insurance Company that, the Tribunal has no jurisdiction to try the petition on hand since petitioners are permanent residents of Andhra Pradesh State and R.C. owner of the vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 is residing at Delhi.
The claim petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act can be initiated in any of the following places.
1) The place where the accident has taken place, 2) the place where the claimants are residing or 3) the place where any one of the respondents in the proceedings is residing or 4) in the place where the policy to offending vehicle is issued from the insurer of the vehicle, as observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in a case reported in 2017 (1) KCCR 511 (Anitha and Others Vs. Ravindranath and Another and, 2). Hanumanth vs Shankar Satappa Wali (WP no:114729-2019), 3) Mantoo Sarkar Vs Oriental Insurance co. Ltd. And others (Civil appeal no 7318-2017 arising out of special leave petition civil no; 18201 0f 2007).
Under these circumstances, the Tribunal has Territorial Jurisdiction to adjudicate the petition on hand.
It is the specific plea of the insurance company that the incident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased.

It is specific plea of the Insurance Company that, the accident is occurred due to contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
No positive evidence is placed on record by Insurance Company to establish that, the incident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased.

the deceased.

26. Even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency,
physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth,
which can never be equated in terms of the money.
Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency.
Hence, Petitioners no:1 to 3 are considered as dependents of deceased.
So, annual income of deceased is taken at Rs.9,52,996/- which would meet the ends of justice.

6 am of the opinion that it would meet the ends of justice if increase in 15% is taken into consideration for determining the income of the deceased.
So, annual income of deceased is taken at Rs.10,95,945/-, which would meet the ends of justice.
opennyai_summary.decision:
By applying the principles of above ruling 15% has to be added to annual income of deceased, which comes to Rs.1,42,949/-.
From this his personal living expenses which should be 1/3rd of Rs.10,95,945/- has to be deducted.
Thereby, the actual annual income will come to Rs.10,95,945 - Rs.3,65,315/- =Rs.7,30,630/-.
28.
As the deceased was 57 years old at the time of death, the multiplier of 09 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.7,30,630/- x 09 = Rs.65,75,670/- for loss of dependency.

Hence, I answer Issue No.4 is in partly affirmative .
In view of discussion made above, I proceed to pass the following.
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.
Petitioners are awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.65,90,670/-
(Rupees Sixty Five Lakhs, Ninety Thousand, Six Hundred and Seventy Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.
Respondent No:2 shall pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the awarded compensation amount to the petitioners in the court within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
: APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60%, petitioner no: 2 and 3 are entitled for 20% each with interest.
50% of share of petitioners with interest is to be paid to them through E-payment,
after due identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 50% of their share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in their names in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years.
